articles.title: DR Congo: DRC: Ebola BVD Outbreak: LTC Situation Report (Telecoms) #9 (Reporting period: 01 - 14 August 2026)
articles.description: Country: Democratic Republic of the Congo Sources: Emergency Telecommunications Cluster, Logistics Cluster, World Food Programme Please refer to the attached file. Summary Points • LTC Telecoms is scaling up telecommunications support for the Ebola response in Bunia, Mongbwalu and Kisangani, providing coordination, connectivity, security communications, power solutions and Information Management (IM) services to enable humanitarian operation. • Security communications capacity is being strengthened across Ituri Province through upgrades to the Security Communications System (SCS), including the arrival of VHF repeater equipment in Bunia that will enhance radio coverage for UN and NGO responders in Bunia and Mongbwalu. • Connectivity capabilities continue to expand, with 20 Starlink Mini units acquired and additional Starlink kits positioned in Kinshasa for deployment to Ebolaaffected areas, supporting reliable communications for response teams.

articles.title: Mali: 6 injured people transferred from Kidal to Gao
articles.description: Country: Mali Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Bamako (ICRC) – On August 16, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) facilitated the medical transfer of six wounded people from the Kidal Referral Health Center (CSREF) to the hospital in Gao. This action, carried out with full transparency thanks to security guarantees obtained from all parties to the conflict, falls within the ICRC's role as a neutral intermediary. “Our role as a neutral intermediary is a fundamental aspect of our mandate,” explains Nicolas Lambert, head of the ICRC delegation in Mali. “ICRC teams were able to successfully transfer the wounded to an appropriate medical institution to receive the additional care necessary for their recovery and ultimately to be reunited with their families.” “For the ICRC, it is essential to ensure that the wounded and sick in conflict-affected areas have access to the necessary medical care,” explains Nicolas Lambert. Thus, in accordance with its mandate, and with the agreement of the health authorities, the ICRC continues to support some twenty community health centers (CSCOMs), the hospitals in Gao and Mopti, as well as referral health centers, benefiting the population by providing essential medical supplies and technical and financial support to healthcare personnel. Between January and June 2026, 69,892 people received care in these various Ministry of Health facilities supported by the ICRC. The ICRC underlines that under international humanitarian law, detainees and the injured must be treated humanely under all circumstances. Measures must be taken to guarantee their safety and dignity during transfers. The ICRC reiterates its commitment to maintaining bilateral, confidential and constructive dialogue with all parties to the conflict. This approach allows the organization to fully carry out its role as a neutral intermediary, acting in the interests of people who are affected or vulnerable, on strictly humanitarian grounds. For more information, please contact: Kany Elizabeth Sogoba, ICRC Bamako, tel: +223 76 99 63 75, email: ksogoba@icrc.org Aminata Cissé, ICRC Bamako, tel: +223 82 99 21 02, email: amicisse@icrc.org Jean Yves Clemenzo, ICRC Geneva, tel: + 41 79 251 93 02, email: jclemenzo@icrc.org
